confirmed.title: Sum-to-1 renormalization over non-exhaustive bucket sets manufactures literal model_prob=1.0 (today's live signal)
confirmed.fallacy_class: certainty-fallacy / probability-mass conservation applied to a partial partition
confirmed.description: bucket_probabilities clamps each bucket to [0.001,0.999] (line 214) then divides by the total so probabilities sum to 1.0 (lines 216-220; same pattern in empirical_bucket_probabilities lines 315-319 and the scipy-less fallback lines 374-381). This renormalization encodes the belief that the buckets passed in exhaust the outcome space. They frequently do not: the S221 thin-market filter (weather_bot.py:1730, _filter_thin_markets at 4536-4582) drops individual sibling buckets on liquidity/volume/spread BEFORE grouping (weather_bot.py:1777), and group_markets (market_mapper.py:584-594) also silently drops buckets on parse failure and builds a group from whatever survives, with no completeness check and no minimum bucket count. The only defense, the M7 coherence check (weather_bot.py:2714), fires only when len(group.buckets) >= 4 — a group stripped to 1-3 buckets bypasses it entirely. Degenerate case: a single surviving bucket with any model p in (0.01, 0.99) renormalizes to p/p = exactly 1.0, silently breaking the 0.999 clamp whose stated purpose is 'avoid 0/1'. This is the only code path that can emit a literal 1.0, and it exactly reproduces today's live signal: model_prob=1.0, price 0.43, edge 0.57=1.0-0.43, at 0.8h lead (with >=2 buckets the 0.001 sibling floors cap the renormalized max below 0.9995). With 2-3 survivors the same math inflates every probability by 1/total, fabricating edge on both YES and NO sides.
confirmed.concrete_harm: A market where the model may actually assign ~40-60% is entered as a certainty: the fabricated 0.57 edge passes the 0.08 min-edge gate, the exec-edge gate (1.0 minus any ask is positive), and the negative-EV gate (capped confidence 0.95 > price 0.43); the Smoczynski-Tomkins allocator consumes the raw 1.0 and computes full Kelly edge f_i=1.0, awarding this bucket the maximum share of the group budget. The bot systematically buys whatever bucket survives the liquidity filter, at whatever price, on structurally thin events — the trade admission itself, its direction, and its allocation are all artifacts of which siblings got filtered, not of any forecast.
confirmed.verify_reasoning: Every element verified in code. (1) probability_engine.py:210-220 clamps each bucket to [0.001,0.999] then divides by the sum when total>0.01 and |total-1|>0.01; same pattern at :313-319 (empirical path, dominant in production at n>=50) and :373-381 (fallback). The divide encodes the belief that the passed-in buckets exhaust the outcome space. (2) They frequently do not: weather_bot.py:1730 runs _filter_thin_markets (per-market drops on liq<$1000/vol<$100/spread>20%, :4544-4582, no sibling awareness) BEFORE group_markets at :1777; market_mapper.py:519-594 additionally drops buckets on city-parse/no-station/bucket-parse failure and builds groups from survivors with no completeness check and no minimum bucket count. (3) The M7 guard at weather_bot.py:2714 fires only when len(group.buckets)>=4 — 1-3 bucket groups bypass it — and it only checks the priced fraction of SURVIVING buckets, so it cannot detect siblings dropped pre-grouping even in >=4-bucket groups. (4) Degenerate arithmetic verified: a single surviving bucket with raw p in (0.01,0.99) gives total=p, |p-1|>0.01, so p/p = exactly 1.0, silently defeating the 0.999 clamp; with >=2 buckets the 0.001 sibling floors keep the max ~0.999, so a literal 1.0 (even at compute_edges' 4-dp rounding, probability_engine.py:421) requires a single-bucket probs dict — matching today's live signal (model_prob=1.0, edge 0.57 = 1.0-0.43). (5) No neutralizer exists: min(0.95, conf) at weather_bot.py:2814 caps only the confidence field; model_prob and edge are stored raw (:2893-2894); the Smoczynski-Tomkins allocator consumes raw opp["model_prob"] (:3061-3071), so p=1.0 gives f_i=(1*b-0)/b=1.0, the maximum Kelly edge and maximum share of group budget; min-edge default 0.08 (:726), penny filter (:2765) and YES 0.85 price cap (:2777) all pass at price 0.43. (6) The codebase itself documents this exact mechanism having fired before: the S222 comment at weather_bot.py:2934-2937 says the removed ungated METAR push "manufactured near-certain YES probabilities (plus artificial NO edges on sibling buckets via renormalization)" — the symptom was patched, the exhaustiveness assumption was not. Critical severity stands: a live signal fired today through this path, and trade admission, direction, and allocation are all artifacts of which siblings survived the liquidity filter.
confirmed.correction: Two corrections, both widening the finding rather than weakening it. (a) probability_engine.py:216-220 is NOT the only code path that can emit a literal 1.0 as claimed: _apply_metar_resolution_day_override renormalizes at weather_bot.py:3021-3025 with no near-1 skip condition and no clamp, so a single-bucket group emits exactly 1.0 through that path UNCONDITIONALLY (whatever the override set — 0.98, 0.97, 0.92 — divides to 1.0). Today's 0.8h-lead signal is inside its <12h window (weather_bot.py:2669), so the METAR renorm is plausibly the final writer of today's 1.0 when METAR data is available; both sites are instances of the identical fallacy (sum-to-1 over a non-exhaustive bucket set) and both need the fix. (b) Scope is broader than the claim's 1-3-bucket framing: because M7 (weather_bot.py:2714) checks only the priced fraction of buckets that survived into the group, groups with >=4 buckets whose thin siblings were dropped pre-grouping (weather_bot.py:1730) also have every probability silently inflated by 1/total with no detection possible at any layer — the manufactured-edge harm applies to all incomplete groups, not just the <=3-bucket M7 bypass. Minor citation nit: the clamp is line 214 and the divide is lines 219-220; the cited :218 is the guard condition line.

confirmed.title: analyze_opportunity is a structural certainty machine: single-bucket call means output is always 0.0, ~0.99+, or exactly 1.0
confirmed.description: analyze_opportunity passes a one-element list [bucket] to bucket_probabilities. Given the sum-to-1 renormalization, the possible outputs are: {} -> model_prob 0.0 (when p<=0.01, via the .get default at line 2033), unchanged p only when p>=0.99 (renorm skipped inside the |total-1|<=0.01 window), or exactly 1.0 for all p in (0.01,0.99). So this method can NEVER return a calibrated intermediate probability — every answer is a near-certainty on one side or the other, and edge=model_prob-yes_price (line 2034) is a fabricated |edge| of either yes_price or 1-yes_price. The confidence field caps at 0.95 (line 2048) which cosmetically masks the 1.0 without fixing edge. The dashboard manual-analysis path (ui/dashboard.py:1760) consumes this method directly, and it is the documented BaseBot fallback for single-market analysis.
confirmed.concrete_harm: Any consumer of the fallback path — operator dashboard evaluation, future base-engine integration, or a debugging session sanity-checking the model — sees a fabricated 40-60 point edge on essentially every weather market it inspects, in a random direction determined by whether raw p fell above or below 0.01. Decisions or code tuned against these outputs (e.g. 'the model sees huge edges, loosen the gate') inherit pure noise dressed as certainty.
confirmed.verify_reasoning: The math is verified line-by-line and exactly as claimed. weather_bot.py:2032 passes a one-element list [bucket] into bucket_probabilities. In probability_engine.py, each bucket p is clamped to [0.001, 0.999] (line 214); with a singleton, total==p, so the normalizer (lines 217-220) fires for any p in (0.01, 0.99) and yields p/p = exactly 1.0; p <= 0.01 hits the degenerate branch (lines 221-231) returning {} which becomes model_prob 0.0 via the .get default at weather_bot.py:2033; only p in [0.99, 0.999] passes through unchanged (inside the |total-1| <= 0.01 tolerance). The output set is precisely {0.0} ∪ {1.0} ∪ [0.99, 0.999] — the method structurally cannot return a calibrated intermediate probability, and edge at line 2034 is fabricated (≈1−yes_price YES or −yes_price NO, direction determined by whether raw p crosses 0.01). The confidence cap min(0.95, ...) at line 2048 masks the 1.0 cosmetically while edge stays fabricated. This is a demonstrably wrong computation (normalization-over-singleton), not merely unvalidated tuning. HOWEVER, the claimed concrete-harm path is mostly neutralized: the ONLY caller in the codebase is ui/dashboard.py:1760, and that caller constructs market_data at lines 1753-1759 with only {id, category, tokens} — no question/title key — so is_weather_market (market_mapper.py:399-402, regex over question/title) returns False and analyze_opportunity exits with None at weather_bot.py:2007-2008 before the singleton call is ever reached (and _extract_city_and_date('') at :2015-2017 would short-circuit again). Live trading never routes here either: BaseBot's loop calls scan_and_trade, and WeatherBot's scan uses full-group analysis at weather_bot.py:2611/2661. So the dashboard never displays these fabricated edges today; the residual harm is latent — any direct/manual invocation with a real market dict (which does carry question text), or any future BaseBot-fallback integration, receives pure fabrication dressed as certainty. That keeps it real but drops it below 'high'.
confirmed.correction: Severity: high → medium (latent, not active). The fallacy is real and the output-set math is exactly right, but the headline harm is overstated: the dashboard consumer (ui/dashboard.py:1760) feeds market_data lacking question/title, so WeatherBot.analyze_opportunity returns None at weather_bot.py:2007 before reaching the singleton bucket_probabilities call — the operator never sees the fabricated edges through any currently-wired path, and today's live model_prob=1.0 signal did NOT come from this method (live path is group-level at :2611/:2661). Two corrections to scope: (1) the real residual exposure is any direct caller passing a well-formed market dict (debug session, future base-engine fallback integration) — that path does produce guaranteed 0.0/1.0 outputs; (2) the live-relevant variant of this same normalization-over-singleton fallacy is elsewhere: both live probability paths share identical singleton-degenerate normalization (probability_engine.py:216-231 parametric, :315-328 empirical), and group_markets (market_mapper.py:512-616) has no minimum-group-size guard — it drops individual buckets on parse failure while keeping the group, so a group shrunk to 1 bucket flows into the live scan and yields model_prob≈1.0 with a fabricated ~1−price edge in production. That singleton-group live path (not analyze_opportunity) is where this fallacy class can actually cost money and deserves the 'high' label; recommend a len(group.buckets)>=2 (or skip-normalization-for-singleton) guard covering both engine paths plus analyze_opportunity.

confirmed.title: '<2h aggressive' certainty window keyed to a fixed 18:00 UTC anchor, not to when the daily max is physically determined
confirmed.fallacy_class: certainty-fallacy / proxy-anchor treated as outcome determination
confirmed.description: Lead time everywhere anchors to 18:00 UTC ('target_noon', weather_bot.py:2516-2520, 2257-2259, 2469-2473). The METAR override's aggressive branch (aggressive = lead_time_hours < 2.0, line 2964) therefore opens at 16:00 UTC — noon EDT, 11am CDT, 9am PDT — and asserts 'daily high is nearly established': 0.98 for at_or_below well below ceiling (2974-2976), 0.92 for in-range (3003-3006), and 0.001 against reaching a floor 1 degree above current max (2989-2991). Climatological time-of-max for US stations is 14:00-17:00 LOCAL — i.e. 19Z-23Z, entirely AFTER the anchor — so these near-certainties are asserted while 3-8 hours of daytime heating remain; for West-Coast stations the premise is off by most of the heating cycle. Today's live signal at '0.8h lead' fired ~17:12Z = early afternoon local, structurally before Tmax. The code comment 'At <2h lead time, daily high is nearly established' (2962) encodes a belief that is true relative to end-of-day but is evaluated against an arbitrary schedule constant. Additionally the bot stops scanning entirely at lead<0 (2521-2522), so it never re-evaluates during the actual Tmax window and cannot learn this assertion class is premature.
confirmed.concrete_harm: The bot sells off (0.001) buckets 1F above the 11am running max and buys 92-98% claims on 'established' highs hours before the physical high occurs; every warm afternoon converts these near-certainty entries into losses, and the sizing consequences are maximal precisely because the asserted probabilities are extreme.
confirmed.verify_reasoning: Every element verified in code. (1) Lead time is anchored to a hardcoded 18:00 UTC constant in three inline copies: weather_bot.py:2257-2259 (precip), 2469-2473 (wind), 2516-2520 (temperature _analyze_group). (2) The METAR override is called at lead<12h (weather_bot.py:2669-2672) passing that 18Z-anchored lead_time; the aggressive branch at :2964 (`aggressive = lead_time_hours < 2.0`) therefore opens at 16:00 UTC = 9-11am local for the fleet's many America/Los_Angeles, America/Phoenix, America/Denver, America/Chicago stations (station_registry.py:79-562) and noon EDT for eastern ones. It then asserts near-certainties about the daily max: 0.98 at_or_below (:2974-2976), 0.001 for at_or_higher buckets just 1 degree above the running max (:2989-2991), 0.92 in-range (:3003-3006), under the comment "daily high is nearly established" (:2962) — while 3-8 hours of daytime heating remain. (3) No neutralizer exists: grep found no minimum-lead gate and no probability cap touching these values; empirically the bot fired a live signal today at model_prob=1.0, lead 0.8h (~17:12Z), proving the pipeline passes them through to sizing. (4) The belief is demonstrably known-wrong within the codebase itself: forecast_client.py:1223-1233 carries an explicit "S102 fix: use station timezone for local noon instead of hardcoded 18:00 UTC" that was never propagated to weather_bot.py's three copies (adjacent-shape miss), and the S222 comment at weather_bot.py:2932-2937 diagnoses the exact same anchor pathology ("<12h window opens pre-dawn local") for the pushes it removed — yet retains the <2h branch on the same broken clock, merely narrowing the window instead of re-deriving it per station timezone. (5) The lead<0 early-return at :2521-2522 (comment calls it "expired market") stops all scanning/L4 re-evaluation at 18Z, so assertions made 16Z-18Z are never re-checked during the actual afternoon Tmax window. Severity high is correct: the mispriced probabilities are extreme (0.98/0.001), they feed Kelly sizing maximally, western stations are worst (premise off by most of the heating cycle), and a live signal fired on this exact path today. Not critical only because the window is 2h/day/station and requires specific bucket geometry relative to the morning running max.
confirmed.correction: Two minor corrections, substance intact. (a) "Climatological time-of-max 19Z-23Z, entirely AFTER the anchor" slightly overstates for EDT stations: 14:00-17:00 EDT = 18Z-21Z, so the window begins AT the 18Z anchor, not entirely after; for CDT/MDT/PDT/MST stations "entirely after" is accurate. The harm claim is unaffected since the aggressive window (16Z-18Z) precedes Tmax at every US station. (b) One of the four aggressive pushes is monotone-safe and should be excluded from the harm: 0.98 for at_or_higher when running_max is already at/near the floor (weather_bot.py:2983-2985) — the max only rises, so that assertion is sound. The genuinely premature assertions are the three non-monotone ones: 0.98 at_or_below (:2974), 0.001 at_or_higher-below-floor (:2989), 0.92 range (:3003). Additional supporting evidence not in the original claim: the codebase already contains the correct fix — forecast_client.py:1223-1233 ("S102 fix: use station timezone for local noon instead of hardcoded 18:00 UTC") — which was never applied to weather_bot.py's three 18Z copies, making this a known-wrong belief retained by omission, not merely an unvalidated one.

confirmed.title: Resolution-source/settlement uncertainty is exactly zero everywhere: the only hook (boundary_risk) is logging-only, removed on contaminated P&L evidence
confirmed.fallacy_class: certainty-fallacy / missing settlement-uncertainty term, tuned on stale ground truth
confirmed.description: The pipeline contains no term anywhere for P(resolution source disagrees with my measurement source). _near_boundary (weather_bot.py:5415-5443) documents the exact failure — 'A 0.5F/C gap between WU and NWS can flip the result — the Dec 2025 NYC incident (WU=29F vs NWS=30F)' — but S121 reduced it to a log line: 'boundary_risk tracked for logging but NO LONGER discounts confidence. Let Kelly self-regulate — the 50% discount was crushing profitable trades' (2807-2810). That removal rationale was a P&L-based tuning decision from the era when the WU scraper was dead and the bot was calibrated against ERA5 fallback (the ground truth itself was wrong), so the 'profitable trades' evidence was contaminated. Meanwhile the METAR override can stand probabilities at 0.97-0.98 and renormalization can reach 1.0: the system claims 30:1 to 1000:1 on outcomes that historically flip on source disagreement at far higher base rates than 0.1-3%. The engine-side clamps (0.001/0.999) are numerical guards against log(0), not calibrated floors reflecting settlement risk — nothing distinguishes 'model is unsure' from 'model is sure but the referee may read a different thermometer'.
confirmed.concrete_harm: Every boundary-adjacent trade is systematically oversized and over-admitted relative to its true win probability; the specific dollar shape is repeated small edges collected until a knife-edge day (the documented 29F-vs-30F class) hits a max-confidence position, and the Brier/calibration telemetry looks fine right up until it doesn't because the miscalibration lives in the settlement layer the model refuses to price.
confirmed.verify_reasoning: Every load-bearing element of the claim checks out in code. (1) boundary_risk is genuinely inert: computed at weather_bot.py:2810, consumed only by logger.debug (2863-2871), inert opp metadata (2902), and event_data telemetry (3721); no sizing/admission/confidence consumer. The _near_boundary docstring (5422) still instructs 'Caller should reduce position size when this flag is True' — violated by its only caller. (2) The removal rationale is P&L-based in the code itself (2808-2809: 'the 50% discount was crushing profitable trades'), and a second independent kill of the same signal (S205 calibrator feature elimination, settings.py:888) also occurred inside the dead-WU/ERA5 ground-truth window — both decisions rest on evidence the operator has designated unreliable. (3) No other settlement-uncertainty term exists: engine clamps (probability_engine.py:214/313/373/597, max(0.001,min(0.999,p))) are log(0) guards; the METAR override (2970-3011) stands hardcoded 0.97/0.98/0.92 with no calibrated basis, and the renormalizer (3021-3027) has NO upper clamp — a single-bucket group yields exactly 1.0 (0.98/0.98), matching today's live model_prob=1.0/edge-0.57 signal. (4) The certainty flows into money at face value: the Smoczynski-Tomkins Kelly allocator uses raw model_prob (3061), not the min(0.95)/0.99-clamped confidence, so p=1.0 gives f_i=1.0 (full Kelly fraction of group budget). Partial mitigants exist but do not neutralize: the METAR unit_margin (2965) protects only the 0.001 rule-out direction (the 0.97 YES-assert at 2986-2988 fires while METAR is still up to 0.5 deg BELOW the floor — anti-conservative against exactly the documented WU-vs-NWS gap); the confidence caps (2814, 685) never touch the model_prob channel; the confidence-tail dampener is default-OFF (settings.py:895); group/city exposure caps (3125-3136) bound the dollar loss per incident but not the epistemic defect. Severity high is correct: this is a demonstrably wrong belief (literal p=1.0 against a 0.43 market, with the flip mechanism documented in the bot's own docstring), not merely unvalidated.
confirmed.correction: Three scope corrections. (1) The '30:1 to 1000:1' framing understates one channel and overstates another: the confidence channel is clamped at 0.95 pre-calibration (weather_bot.py:2814) and 0.99 post (685), but the channel that actually sizes trades — the S-T Kelly allocator at 3061 — uses RAW model_prob, which after the unclamped METAR renormalization (3021-3027) can reach literal 1.0 (infinite implied odds) for single-bucket groups; today's live 1.0 signal is exactly this path, and at p=1.0 Kelly allocates its full fraction. (2) One direction of the METAR override DOES carry a crude settlement-source guard: the 0.001 rule-outs require running_max to exceed the bound by unit_margin (0.5F/0.3C, matching the documented WU-vs-NWS gap). The missing-term fallacy is concentrated in the YES-asserts (0.97 at running_max >= low_bound - 0.5, i.e. before the floor is crossed on METAR) and in the base CDF path. (3) Concrete harm is bounded, not open-ended: kelly_mult=0.25 x group_budget plus group/city exposure caps (3125-3136) cap per-incident loss — the shape is systematic bounded oversizing plus over-admission (edge=1.0-price passes every gate and feeds the boost stack), not account-level blowup on one knife-edge day. Additionally, post-2026-07-01 the EMOS sigma re-learning vs real WU will implicitly fold some settlement scatter into the base-path distribution — but that mitigant is bypassed precisely where the certainty claims originate (the METAR override at lead<12h).

confirmed.title: Ungated 0.97 YES push fires when the threshold has NOT been crossed (running_max still 0.5 below floor), with a unit-inconsistent margin
confirmed.description: In _apply_metar_resolution_day_override, the at_or_higher branch sets P=0.97 at ANY lead <12h when 'running_max >= bucket.low_bound - 0.5' (2986-2988) — i.e. when the observed max is up to half a degree BELOW the market threshold. The 0.97 encodes two stacked assumptions as near-certainty: (a) the resolution source will round half-up from the exact METAR/ASOS value (a 54.5 reading resolves a '55 or higher' market YES), and (b) the resolution source's reading equals the METAR T-group value to within the margin. Both are boundary/rounding coin-flips, not 32:1 events — and the WU-vs-METAR chain involves independent C-to-F conversion and per-source rounding. confirmed.concrete_harm: The freshly-enabled exit path will systematically hold overpriced losers-in-waiting and liquidate underpriced positions at a model-assessed discount — value transfer to counterparties on every exit decision where price has moved away from entry.

Decision-theoretically, entry price is sunk; the correct hold-vs-sell comparison is fresh model value vs. current price. Both error branches verified in code: (a) HOLDs model-overpriced tokens (no other code path sells a winner whose market price exceeds model value — hard stop only fires on losses); (b) SELLs at a discount to model value when fresh_prob dropped >0.05 below entry while current_price < fresh_prob. confirmed.correction: Severity medium is correct, but two scope corrections: (1) The claim's second example (entry 0.70, current 0.35 = −50% pnl) would be intercepted by the shared inviolable hard stop BEFORE the mid-life EV test — check_hard_stop_loss (bots/weather/engine/base_engine/risk/risk_manager.py:681-699, WB default −25% price move) runs first at weather_bot.py:4061-4066 and fires regardless of the mid-life flag.
